q1_issues.issue: The forecast range is asserted at top level (statements 5-7), so the parse claims revenue of $8.1-8.7 billion actually holds, when the text says only that Intel expects it.
(Time sk_expect_1 fourth_quarter) puts the quarter on the expecting event, but "for the fourth quarter" says which period the revenue falls in, not when the expecting happens.

The measure shape is inverted: revenue is the dimension the instruction set puts in the scale slot (as "costs $20" gives price on the thing priced), yet here it is both the measured entity's class and its own scale.

q2_gaps: An intensional / forecast NP object of an attitude verb ("expects revenue between X and Y") — the entity-object route is defined for referents that exist independently ("fears the dog") and sealing is finite-clause-only, so a predicted quantity has no encoding that avoids asserting the prediction.

Scale words in a monetary magnitude ("$8.1 billion") — unit is specified as a lemmatized singular (dollar) with no rule for million/billion, so the parse coins billion_dollar, which no canonical-unit conversion reaches.
A two-sided range ("between X and Y") has no stated form; pairing MeasureAtLeast with MeasureAtMost is a reasonable composition but is nowhere licensed as the range encoding.
notes: Experiencer / Stimulus on expect follows the attitude-verb routing, and fourth_quarter as a bare named-time constant matches the deictic-constant convention.
